title: Pautalia · the public thermae
figure: Fig. 50 · after Ruseva-Slokoska 2002: 44, fig. 2 · Avramova 2024, digital p. 296 / printed p. 292
scope: A source-traced relief of the published public-thermae plan: clearly bounded internal partitions, recorded boundary linework, the seven arcade alignments in room 1 and individually legible support marks in rooms 3 and 4. The city plan and eastern reservoir are not combined into this model.
limitation: Plan geometry is distinguished by evidence: filled partitions have two legible edges; copper outlines show drafting lines whose wall thickness is unknown; low details show the recorded hypocaust alignments and support marks. All relief heights are display conventions, not ancient elevations. Fig. 51 provides partial hypocaust sections but does not establish whole-building elevations. No roof, completed arch system, bath water, missing pillar rows or unexcavated continuation is reconstructed. Keep the source visible for direct comparison.

features.label: Recorded partition bands
features.note: The filled bands follow partitions with two legible edges in Fig. 50. Door interruptions and the narrow southern crossing remain open. The source does not establish original elevations; the displayed relief height is not a measurement.

features.label: Room 1 · seven arcade alignments
features.note: Seven parallel arcade alignments are visible in Fig. 50 and described on dissertation printed p. 89. Only their recorded plan extents are raised, including the short eastern surviving trace. These are projected alignments, not seven solid Roman walls; arches and unexcavated continuations are not reconstructed.

features.label: Rooms 3 & 4 · surviving support marks
features.note: Each small footprint follows an individually visible support mark in Fig. 50. The plate distinguishes the extant concentration from empty or unrecorded areas; no missing rows have been completed. These are the support marks shown by the draughtsperson, not an archaeological inventory or measured column heights. Printed p. 91 describes both brick-tile and ceramic-cylinder pilae, so a uniform upper cylinder is not invented.

features.label: Recorded plan boundaries
features.note: Copper lines trace the source draughtsperson’s boundaries, including outlines whose exterior wall edge or thickness is not recoverable. Their consistent 1.8-pixel draft stroke is a display convention, not a wall dimension. Page frames, oblique section/cut lines and printed room numbers are excluded.

features.label: Uncompleted internal traces
features.note: Fine lines preserve short source traces in rooms 2, 4 and 9 without joining their open ends or assigning functions. They are drafted linework rather than assertions of solid masonry.

features.label: Room 1 · transverse traces
features.note: The short transverse divisions are copied where visible south of the seven arcade alignments. No height, bridging arch or connection beyond a recorded end is inferred.

features.label: Northern recorded fragments
features.note: Fragmentary northern boundaries follow the source strokes without closing unexcavated gaps. The staircase is retained in the flat source plate; no stair risers or elevations are invented.

features.label: Source profiles marked a
features.note: These small semicircular profiles are retained as drawn lines. Their labels are left in the source plate, and they are not interpreted as new pools, rooms or measured vaults.

traceMethod: Manual reading of architectural bands and source linework in image coordinates. Small support bounds were detected in the original raster and individually checked in an enlarged overlay; six clearly readable markers attached to the partition were added manually. Rendered page frame, oblique source section/cut lines, arrows, room numbers and labels are not raised.
supportingSources: Avramova 2024, digital p. 93 / printed p. 89: room-1 hypocaust, seven parallel arcades, partial excavation beneath the Ottoman mosque.
Avramova 2024, digital p. 95 / printed p. 91: brick-tile and ceramic-cylinder supports in rooms 3 and 4.
